parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/app.ts belongs to the infrastructure layer, and everything it does fits that role. It sets up the Express HTTP adapter and acts as the composition root, wiring together the domain Catalogue, OrderService and CatalogueService. Each route handler does transport work only: it reads request params, query and body, makes simple shape checks (the items array is non-empty, state is present), calls application services, and turns results and exceptions into HTTP status codes and JSON. The handlers contain no business rules such as pricing, stock checks or order state transitions; those are left to the application/domain services. Seeding the sample products at startup is bootstrap fixture data run through the application service, not domain logic. That is a reasonable composition-root concern, though it is the most debatable item here. The file does no persistence or domain logic that belongs to another layer kind.
